Loading history… Monday, August 10th Gautam Talks    4:51 PM Not a feature request, but hopefully useful. I spent a few weeks benchmarking Firecracker guest images and published the harnesses: github.com/GautamTalksDev/mayfly-guest Main finding: most published kernel-stripping advice for Firecracker is stale. Turning ACPI off costs 278ms rather than saving time, because modern Firecracker passes device info through ACPI tables and MPTable booting is now deprecated. Disabling PCI breaks root disk

nodes.directText: Heads up: spot sandboxes are preemptible. They can be reclaimed at any time when on-demand capacity is needed, so design workloads to tolerate interruption. Preempted sandboxes get a timestamp and stay retrievable for 24 hours. Try it: Docs
nodes.subtreeText: Heads up: spot sandboxes are preemptible. They can be reclaimed at any time when on-demand capacity is needed, so design workloads to tolerate interruption. Preempted sandboxes get a spotEvictedAt timestamp and stay retrievable for 24 hours. Try it: https://app.daytona.io/ Docs: https://www.daytona.io/docs/sandboxes#spot-gpu-sandboxes Questions? Drop them here or at support@daytona.io

nodes.subtreeText: 3:07 How we support static egress IPs: The recommended approach is to use a VPN connection with Tailscale and route your sandbox traffic through an exit node you control with a known static IP. From your firewall's perspective, all sandbox traffic will originate from that single IP — giving you full control over what to allowlist. This works out of the box in Daytona since Tailscale falls back to TCP when UDP isn't available. Full guide here: daytona.io/docs/en/vpn-connections#…
